description: issue #775 (review gate, QA finding B2): `wait "-1"` -- the RANGE arm of `wait`'s tick count reached through a WORD. `spec/interaction-events.md`'s `### wait <n>` requires a non-negative whole number and raises `ol-range` on a negative one; `spec/execution-model.md:33-34` makes "words that parse as numbers are accepted where a number is expected" a normative CORE rule, so `"-1"` MUST reach that `ol-range` exactly as the literal `-1` does (pinned by the sibling `wait-negative`). Nothing covered the composition of those two rules: every RANGE fixture passed a number literal, so an implementation that trusted the type check to have already handled words -- guarding the range only when the argument was literally a number -- would let `wait "-1"` SUCCEED silently, emitting the trailing `primitive` event as though a pause had run. For a pause primitive that is an invisible wrong result rather than an error, and it survived a fully green run until this fixture existed (found by mutation). Note `params.value` is the COERCED number `-1`, not the word `"-1"` -- the opposite of the `ol-type` arm (`wait-non-whole-word`), and deliberately so: `ol-range` is a question about magnitude, which only exists after coercion, while `ol-type` is a question about what the learner actually wrote. As with every other failed `wait` validation the `primitive` event is NOT emitted, only the instruction event precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the argument.

diagnostics.message: wait needs a count of 0 or greater, but got -1.
